name: Pickands-Balkema-de Haan, forward direction
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.exists_tendstoUniformlyOn_excessSurvival_of_isInMDAGEV'
  (F : CumulativeDistributionFunction) {ξ : ℝ} (hF : F.IsInMDAGEV ξ) :
  ∃ β,
    (∀ᶠ (u : ℝ) in F.upperEndpointFilter, 0 < β u) ∧
      TendstoUniformlyOn
        (fun u x =>
          ExtremeValueTheory.excessSurvival (fun y => 1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction y) u (β u * x))
        (ExtremeValueTheory.gpdSurvivalAll ξ 1) F.upperEndpointFilter (Set.Ici 0)
scope_note: Only the direction domain of attraction => GPD limit. The equivalence is pbdh.

name: Pickands-Balkema-de Haan theorem
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isInMDAGEV_iff_exists_tendstoUniformlyOn_excessSurvival
  (F : CumulativeDistributionFunction) (ξ : ℝ) :
  F.IsInMDAGEV ξ ↔
    ∃ β,
      (∀ᶠ (u : ℝ) in F.upperEndpointFilter, 0 < β u) ∧
        TendstoUniformlyOn
          (fun u x =>
            ExtremeValueTheory.excessSurvival (fun y => 1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction y) u (β u * x))
          (ExtremeValueTheory.gpdSurvivalAll ξ 1) F.upperEndpointFilter (Set.Ici 0)
scope_note: Equivalence for every xi, with an arbitrary eventually positive scale. Written after the change of variable x -> beta(u) x, so the GPD has scale 1 and x ranges over [0, infinity) rather than (0, x_F - u).

name: Pickands-Balkema-de Haan, Fréchet case
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isInMDAFrechet_iff_tendstoUniformlyOn_excessSurvival
  (F : CumulativeDistributionFunction) {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) :
  F.IsInMDAFrechet hα ↔
    TendstoUniformlyOn
      (fun u x =>
        ExtremeValueTheory.excessSurvival (fun y => 1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction y) u (u / α * x))
      (ExtremeValueTheory.gpdSurvivalNonneg (1 / α) 1) Filter.atTop (Set.Ici 0)
scope_note: xi > 0 only, with the canonical scale beta(u) = u/alpha on both sides: the converse is weaker than the book's, which allows any scale.

name: Pickands-Balkema-de Haan, Weibull case
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.isInMDAWeibull_iff_tendstoUniformlyOn_excessSurvival
  (F : CumulativeDistributionFunction) {α : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) :
  F.IsInMDAWeibull hα ↔
    ∃ xF,
      ↑F.toStieltjesFunction xF = 1 ∧
        (∀ x < xF, ↑F.toStieltjesFunction x < 1) ∧
          TendstoUniformlyOn
            (fun u x =>
              ExtremeValueTheory.excessSurvival (fun y => 1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction y) u
                ((xF - u) / α * x))
            (ExtremeValueTheory.gpdSurvivalAll (-1 / α) 1) (nhdsWithin xF (Set.Iio xF)) (Set.Ici 0)
scope_note: xi < 0 only, with the canonical scale beta(u) = (x_F - u)/alpha on both sides: the converse is weaker than the book's.

name: Pickands-Balkema-de Haan, Gumbel case
statement:
CumulativeDistributionFunction.tendstoUniformlyOn_excessSurvival_of_auxiliary
  (F : CumulativeDistributionFunction) {L : Filter ℝ} {f : ℝ → ℝ} (hf : ∀ᶠ (u : ℝ) in L, 0 < f u)
  (h :
    ∀ (x : ℝ),
      0 ≤ x →
        Filter.Tendsto
          (fun t => (1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction (t + x * f t)) / (1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction t)) L
          (nhds (Real.exp (-x)))) :
  TendstoUniformlyOn
    (fun u x =>
      ExtremeValueTheory.excessSurvival (fun y => 1 - ↑F.toStieltjesFunction y) u (f u * x))
    (ExtremeValueTheory.gpdSurvivalAll 0 1) L (Set.Ici 0)
scope_note: xi = 0 only, and it starts from an auxiliary function rather than from the domain of attraction. The existence of the auxiliary function is a hypothesis here.

name: Pickands-Balkema-de Haan, Fréchet forward direction for a survival function
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.tendstoUniformlyOn_excessSurvival {F : ℝ → ℝ} {α : ℝ}
  (hF : Antitone F) (hRV : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying F (-α)) (hα : 0 < α) :
  TendstoUniformlyOn (fun u x => ExtremeValueTheory.excessSurvival F u (u / α * x))
    (ExtremeValueTheory.gpdSurvivalNonneg (1 / α) 1) Filter.atTop (Set.Ici 0)
scope_note: Forward direction, xi > 0 only, with the explicit scale u/alpha, for an antitone regularly varying function.

name: Mean excess of a regularly varying tail
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.tendsto_meanExcess_div {F : ℝ → ℝ} {α : ℝ} (hF : Antitone F)
  (hRV : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying F (-α)) (hα : 1 < α) :
  Filter.Tendsto (fun u => ExtremeValueTheory.meanExcess F u / u) Filter.atTop (nhds (1 / (α - 1)))
scope_note: F antitone, which holds for a survival function. meanExcess is the formula (integral of F over (u, infinity))/F(u), which equals E[X - u | X > u] when F is a survival function.

name: The GPD mean excess function is linear
scope_note: xi < 1 and u in the support. As in mean-excess-rv, the mean excess is the integral formula.

name: A linear mean excess characterizes the GPD
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.eq_gpdSurvivalAll_of_meanExcess_eq_linear {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ}
  [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] {a b : ℝ} (ha : 0 < a) (hb : 0 ≤ b)
  (hS : ∀ (u : ℝ), 0 ≤ u → 0 < μ.real (Set.Ioi u))
  (he :
    ∀ (u : ℝ), 0 ≤ u → ExtremeValueTheory.meanExcess (fun t => μ.real (Set.Ioi t)) u = a + b * u)
  {u : ℝ} (hu : 0 ≤ u) :
  μ.real (Set.Ioi u) =
    μ.real (Set.Ioi 0) * ExtremeValueTheory.gpdSurvivalAll (b / (1 + b)) (a / (1 + b)) u
scope_note: Unbounded support only (slope b >= 0, positive tail on [0, infinity)): shapes xi < 0 are left out, and it describes the tail beyond 0, not the law.

name: Strong consistency of the empirical mean excess function
source: no number cited in the library
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.ae_tendsto_empMeanExcess.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω}
  {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ]
  {X : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} (hX : ∀ (i : ℕ), ProbabilityTheory.HasLaw (X i) μ P)
  (hind : ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun X P) (hpos : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => max x 0) μ)
  {u : ℝ} (hu : 0 < μ.real (Set.Ioi u)) :
  ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂P,
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ExtremeValueTheory.empMeanExcess (fun i => X i ω) n u) Filter.atTop
      (nhds (ExtremeValueTheory.meanExcess (fun t => μ.real (Set.Ioi t)) u))
scope_note: A fixed threshold u; iid data. Uniformity in u and behaviour as u grows with n are not stated.
